children: said on Wednesday it had approved raising of funds worth 55 billion rupees ($588.6 million) as the cash-strapped Indian carrier seeks to strengthen its finances after prolonged operational and regulatory challenges.

The fundraise, which may include equity and other permitted instruments, comes as the budget airline struggles with a prolonged cash crunch that has forced it to ground aircraft, cut flights and delay salaries.
The airline said the funds would help ease liquidity pressures, strengthen its balance sheet, restore flights, support fleet expansion and meet operational needs.
SpiceJet has also delayed regulatory filings, prompting an Indian stock exchange to warn about a potential trading suspension if overdue financial results are not submitted by December 7.
